result.csv must have exactly the columns [id, invest, defer, benefit, cost] in that order, with string-typed rows. check_case reads it via pandas.read_csv(dtype=str), asserts list(g.columns)==list(w.columns) (rejecting added, dropped, or reordered columns) and asserts every column is non-numeric (string-typed). C-5c7fbe9f.evidence: The IPv4 pattern must accept only decimal octets 0..255 with no leading zeros and must not match inside a longer alphanumeric token. Hidden case b plants OUT_OF_RANGE (256/999) and LEADING_ZERO (010) decoys and hidden case c plants a token x192.0.2.1y; every occurrence is counted via the pattern, so a permissive/loose pattern (verified: replacing the octet with [0-9]{1,3} makes the visible value go from 8 to 9 and fails) or a boundary-blind one changes total_hits/distinct and fails test.sh on visible/a/b/c.

willow-bridge: verifier executes /app/jupyter_server_config.py, /app/ipv4_octet.awk on the visible fixture and on independent hidden cases (tests/hidden); an agent lacking 'match an ipv4 octet pattern without leading zeros' cannot produce artifacts that pass those checks.

C-188767ed.evidence: The verifier replays the reference validation-and-transfer rule (reject unknown parties / same party / unknown asset / asset-not-owned-by-seller; otherwise debit the buyer by the asset price, credit the seller, reassign item ownership to the buyer, and append an approved log entry) against each case's initial ledger and asserts the final balances, final ownership, and ordered transfer_log in result.json match that recomputation on /app/data and on every hidden case. Hidden h1 chains transfers so an asset rejected in an early row becomes eligible again only after a later row reassigns its owner; h1/h2/h3 also plant unknown-party, same-party, unknown-asset and not-owned rows. Wrong debit/credit direction, a skipped reassignment, or a log emitted out of row order changes the state and fails (a no-ownership-update solver fails 7 checks on the baseline and 10 on h1).

Verifier 'transfer rule mismatch' check runs /verifier side reference that negotiates the documented validate-and-transfer rule and requires out/transfer_out.json (balances, ownership, appended log) to match exactly. Approving an invalid transfer, applying debit/credit in the wrong direction, failing to reassign item ownership, or failing to append the log entry yields state that differs from the reference -> fails. Hidden cases include approved, invalid-owner, and non-positive-amount transfers.

C-410d591c.evidence: check.py recomputes boolean columns, per-group count, per-numeric-column sum and mean (rounded to 6dp), and per-boolean-column truth counts, and asserts all of them plus the exact boolean_columns list against result.json for the baseline and the three hidden cases. Hidden h1 keeps booleans as real numbers (1/0) mixed with true/false words; hidden h2/h3 include numeric columns whose values would be confusing (9.75, 2) that a naive bool-tester must not class as boolean. C-50a4f9fe.evidence: check.py recomputes the completed tide series (linear interpolation by hour between the nearest available readings, leading-gap clamp to the first available value, trailing-gap clamp to the last available value, a fully-empty port left empty) and compares every filled cell within 1e-3 plus row ordering. Hidden h1/h3 exercise interior, leading-only, trailing-only, repeated-hour, and fully-empty ports; a misindexed fill or wrong edge fallback flips a value at a flagged position and fails.

C-50a576ef.evidence: check.py re-parses DTSTART/DTEND of every VEVENT in each *.ics file and asserts the slots mapping (ISO YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, identical repeats collapsed to one, a VEVENT missing its DTEND dropped, malformed lines ignored) equals the slots list in result.json. Hidden h1 includes duplicate intervals that must collapse and a trailing VEVENT without DTEND; hidden h3 embeds garbage and an undated DTSTART. A mis-parsed time token, a duplicate pair kept twice, or a missing-end event counted changes the ordering and fails.

calendar_blocks must expose each VEVENT's parsed DTSTART/DTEND pair for every .ics file, and availability must answer whether a candidate window overlaps the parsed blocking intervals. The grader recomputes both and enforces half-open overlap semantics (probe == block end is free, verified in hidden 'a' and 'c'), drops VEVENTs missing DTEND (hidden 'a'), and treats unknown calendars as fully free (hidden 'a'). A mis-parsed time token or a wrong interval comparison flips an availability boolean and fails.

C-58b99c97.evidence: check.py recounts url frequencies from surge.tsv, sorts by count descending then url ascending, truncates to the top 3, and requires top.tsv lines to match exactly. Hidden h1 places a rank-3/rank-4 tie at the cutoff, so a wrong tie-break or off-by-one truncation selects the wrong third url (fails 2 checks); hidden h2 has only two distinct urls so a hard-coded top-3 / overlong list fails there too; the baseline data also covers a mid-list tie. Delivered /app/download.py reads manifest.json from a public S3-style object endpoint over the loopback HTTP socket, downloads every parquet split by key, SHA-256 verifies each object against the manifest, validates that parquet columns equal manifest['columns'], and assembles train.parquet/val.parquet/test.parquet plus report.json (sha_ok, per-split row counts, total_rows, columns, splits_complete, requiring at least one train and one test split). The verifier re-runs it unchanged against the visible endpoint (bucket moorings) and against three fresh hidden object stores hosting different datasets (different buckets, column sets, counts and sha256s); it recomputes the sha256 of each downloaded split from the hidden source-of-truth bytes, confirms equality, and validates every report figure and merged parquet row count. Byte or schema mismatch fails the hidden case, so a hardcoded-to-visible implementation cannot pass.

C-85b852db.evidence: /app/vector.out is a plain ASCII vector file whose exact content is pinned: line 1 = coefficient count d, then d one-per-line coefficients (10 decimals) and a final intercept line. test.sh parses it and asserts int(count)==len(coef), the d weights match the model's coef to atol 1e-3, and the last float equals the model intercept on the visible and all hidden runs. Anything non-numeric, mis-sized, or not matching the fitted model fails.

The executed toolchain's result is persisted as a real file and re-read by the verifier: /app/all.bc is the persisted linked bitcode that test.sh disassembles and greps, and elf.py/solver.py emit verbatim result text (the address->word JSON and the sat/unsat verdict) that the verifier parses and compares exactly. The numeric word sequences must match the reference decoding byte-for-byte, so a solver that does not actually run the work but prints prebaked text fails on the hidden ELFs and on the unsat query.

C-a74eff68.evidence: /app/train.py prints a per-check self-test (SELFTEST driver_coef=... PASS, SELFTEST val_accuracy=... PASS) plus a mean statistic line SELFTEST MEAN_ACC=<float>. test.sh requires at least two PASS-tagged lines and a MEAN_ACC that is parseable and in [0,1] on every visible and hidden run; a missing/FAIL-only report fails format validation.

The verifier runs python3 /app/selfcheck.py and parses its stdout: requires >=4 lines matching ^CHK: <name>: PASS/FAIL, at least one PASS, and numeric MEAN: and STD: decimal lines — a self-test that omits the tokens or emits non-numeric/no stats fails the format validation regardless of internal behavior.

C-ae9e103e.evidence: The harness loads the persisted /app/model.joblib (coef, intercept, feature_names), rebuilds the fixed StratifiedKFold split from the config (seed/n_folds/held_out_fold) on the CSV, runs forward inference (X@w+b>=0) on the held-out fold, and independently asserts accuracy >= the config's accuracy_floor for the visible and the two full-training hidden cases (h1, h2). Weak or over/under-fit models that miss the floor fail.

C-d06efab8.evidence: train.py takes every path (data, output dir, log dir), split/fold control, accuracy floor, the designated signed feature, and a debug one-epoch override from a YAML config and accepts --data/--out/--logs overrides. In the verifier the same /app/train.py (never reading tests) reruns unchanged on three hidden scenarios with different columns/targets/junk columns to drop, different folds/seeds/floors and a one-epoch debug config; the feature set is rebuilt from the model's own feature_names (with junk columns dropped), so hardcoded paths or feature indexes break.

The verifier statically requires solve.py to read sys.argv and to contain no hard-coded /app paths, and it then executes solve.py against the three fresh hidden fixture trees (distinct directories, synonym maps, includes, weights and CSVs) with paths supplied only via its four CLI arguments. A solver that hard-codes the shipped /app/project, /app/weights.json or /app/inputs.csv paths, or that does not thread all four args through, fails the static checks and/or every hidden runtime check.
